name: Medienkunst / Mediengestaltung (Media Art and Design)
status_note: Program missing from enhanced_german_art_schools.json — only the BFA variant exists there. Needs to be added. Note: runs as two parallel variants — German-taught MFA Medienkunst/Mediengestaltung and English-taught MFA Media Art and Design (MAD).

details.tuitionNote: No tuition fees; semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) only
details.languageRequirements: German variant: German C2. English variant (MAD): German A2 + English C1 (TOEFL >= 95 or IELTS >= 7.0); a large portion of projects and Fachmodule are taught in German even in the English variant — only Interface Design is fully English-taught
details.admission: First professional degree (e.g. BFA in media art/design or equivalent) plus aptitude examination based on artistic portfolio; artistic approval valid for 2 academic years
applicationDocuments: artistic portfolio (PDF max 20MB or hosted links)
motivation letter (one A4 page, stating specialization)

structure: Professorship-based (Klassenprinzip): 2-semester core for holders of an 8-semester / 240-ECTS bachelor (semester 1: master project module at a chosen Professur, 18 ECTS, plus two Fachmodule; semester 2: master thesis, 30 ECTS, plus master colloquium), extended by 1 bridge semester for 210-ECTS and 2 bridge semesters for 180-ECTS bachelors, drawing on the BFA module catalogues (Medienkunst/Mediengestaltung, Visuelle Kommunikation, Produktdesign).

chairs.name: Acoustic Ecologies and Sound Studies
chairs.focus: Sound studies and acoustic ecologies (chair added after the 2022 module handbook; not yet reflected there)

chairs.name: Elektroakustische Komposition und Klangkunst (Electroacoustic Composition and Sound Art)
chairs.focus: Electroacoustic and acousmatic music, sound installation, live electronics, net music, sound art, multimedia; computer as instrument shaped by the composer-performer
modules: Aufnahme- und Tonstudiotechnik I+II (with HfM Franz Liszt Weimar)

chairs.name: Experimentelles Radio (Experimental Radio)
chairs.focus: Radio art and radio practice: live radio plays (Hörspiel), radio installations, festival radios and radio events in urban space, cooperation with public broadcasters; multichannel production, ambisonics, sound in VR

chairs.name: Gestaltung Medialer Umgebungen (Design of Media Environments)
chairs.focus: Sensor-based spatial interaction, motion tracking and computer vision, data streams in image and sound, surveillance and the social impact of data collection, virtual/generated environments, science & art, bioart, art-technology, ethics of new technologies

chairs.name: Interface Design
chairs.focus: Experimental and interactive interfaces, interactive room installations, AR and mobile interaction, ubiquitous and networked technologies, prototyping, physical computing, user- and task-centered design methods, artistic research; linked to the Media Architecture program of the Faculty of Architecture and Urbanism; the only fully English-taught chair

chairs.name: Medien-Ereignisse (Media Events)
chairs.focus: Designing media events: PR and art actions, festivals, social interventions staged publicly; performative-scenographic approaches plus journalistic-documentary formats for web, TV, cinema, exhibition

chairs.name: Kunst und soziale Praxis / Kunst und sozialer Raum
chairs.focus: Professionalization of artistic careers (artist statement, portfolio); collection, inventory and exhibition practices, archives, encyclopedias, Wunderkammern, museography, institutional critique. Present in the 2022 module handbook but no longer listed among the six chairs on the current program page.

theoretical_orientation: art-historical contextualization of one's own artistic position
ethical and socio-political reflection of technology
interdisciplinary dialogue between art and science
pedagogy: Project-based studio work in professor-led classes (18 SWS project modules, 540h workload), plenums and colloquia, public presentation and documentation of artistic work required in nearly every module; modules from other programs of the university can be integrated; cooperation with Hochschule für Musik Franz Liszt Weimar for studio technique.
embedding_text: MFA Medienkunst/Mediengestaltung (Media Art and Design) at Bauhaus-Universität Weimar, offered as a German-taught and a parallel English-taught (MAD) variant. A professorship-based, project-driven media art master where students join one of six chairs: Acoustic Ecologies and Sound Studies (Kerstin Ergenzinger), Electroacoustic Composition and Sound Art (Maximilian Marcoll — acousmatic music, sound installation, live electronics, net music, computer music with Max/MSP, SuperCollider, CSound), Experimental Radio (Nathalie Singer — radio art, live Hörspiel, radio events in urban space, ambisonics, sound in VR), Design of Media Environments (Ursula Damm — sensor-based spatial interaction, motion tracking, computer vision, surveillance and datafication critique, virtual space and game engines, science & art and bioart), Interface Design (Martin Hesselmeier — experimental interfaces, interactive room installations, augmented reality, physical computing with Arduino, web-based interaction, ubiquitous technologies, artistic research), and Media Events (Wolfgang Kissel — performative public events, PR and art actions, social interventions, documentary formats for web, TV, cinema and exhibition). Teaching is studio- and project-based with public presentation, art-historical contextualization, and ethical reflection of new technologies. Two-semester core after a 240-ECTS bachelor, extendable with bridge semesters; winter intake, portfolio-based aptitude examination, no tuition fees.
